title: What Is the Humidity in San Diego?
h1: What Is the Humidity Like in San Diego, and How Does It Affect Your Home?
description: San Diego humidity changes a lot between the coast and inland areas. Learn how marine layer moisture and dry Santa Ana winds affect your home and comfort.
quick_answer: San Diego's humidity depends on where you live and the time of year. Coastal neighborhoods often feel damp, especially on marine layer mornings in late spring and early summer. Inland areas are usually drier. During Santa Ana winds, humidity can drop very low across the county. Indoors, aim for roughly 30 to 50 percent.
body:
San Diego isn't muggy like a tropical climate, and it isn't bone-dry like the desert. It's somewhere in between, and it swings a lot depending on geography and weather. That's why two homes twenty minutes apart can have completely different moisture problems.

Why is the coast more humid than inland areas?

The Pacific Ocean feeds moist air onshore, especially overnight and in the morning. In late spring and early summer, the marine layer often settles over coastal communities and lingers into the afternoon. Homes in beach areas and neighborhoods near bays and lagoons sit in that damp air for long stretches.

As you move inland, the air dries out and warms up. Inland valleys see hotter summer days and cooler nights, with lower humidity during the day. Foothill areas can be drier still.

What happens during Santa Ana winds?

Santa Ana winds blow hot, dry air from the interior toward the coast, usually in fall and winter. Humidity can drop sharply in a matter of hours. These conditions bring fire danger, and they also affect your home:

  • Dry skin, irritated eyes, sore throats and static shocks
  • Wood floors, cabinets and furniture can shrink or crack
  • Dust and pollen get blown into homes through gaps and open windows
  • Wildfire smoke can follow, which makes filtration more important

How does coastal humidity affect your home?

In damp coastal air, moisture tends to build up indoors, especially in homes that are closed up a lot. Watch for these signs:

  • Condensation on windows on cool mornings
  • A musty smell in closets, bathrooms or the garage
  • Mildew spots on bathroom ceilings, window frames or behind furniture on outside walls
  • Clothes, towels and shoes that never quite feel dry
  • Rust on metal fixtures and corrosion on the outdoor AC unit from salt air

Older stucco homes with limited ventilation and single-pane windows are especially prone to these problems.

What indoor humidity should you aim for?

For most homes, roughly 30 to 50 percent indoor humidity is comfortable and healthy. Staying under about 60 percent helps keep mold and dust mites in check. Going much below 30 percent can feel dry and uncomfortable.

A simple hygrometer, which costs very little at a hardware store, will tell you where your home sits. Check it in a few rooms and at different times of day, since bathrooms and kitchens run higher.

How can you control humidity in a San Diego home?

The right fix depends on which direction you need to go.

If your home is too damp

  • Run bathroom exhaust fans during showers and for 15 to 20 minutes after
  • Use the kitchen range hood when cooking
  • Make sure the dryer vent exhausts outside and isn't clogged
  • Run the AC on warm days, since it removes moisture as it cools
  • Consider a whole-home or portable dehumidifier for persistent dampness

If your home is too dry

  • Use a portable humidifier in bedrooms during Santa Ana events
  • Keep windows closed and run the HVAC fan with a good filter on windy, smoky days
  • Consider a whole-home humidifier if dryness is a regular problem, especially inland

Does humidity change through the year?

Yes, and it helps to know the pattern. Late spring and early summer bring the most marine layer days near the coast, so that's when coastal homes feel dampest. Late summer can bring muggy spells when tropical moisture drifts up from the south, even inland. Fall and winter are when Santa Ana winds are most common, bringing the driest air of the year. Winter rain adds moisture for a few days at a time, then things dry out again.

When should you get help with humidity?

If you see recurring mold, constant condensation or musty odors that don't go away, it's worth having someone check your ventilation, ductwork and HVAC system. A leaky return duct in the attic or garage can pull in damp or dusty air. Our indoor air quality team can look at the whole picture and recommend dehumidifiers, humidifiers or ventilation fixes that fit your home.
faqs: Is San Diego considered a humid city?

Not compared to truly muggy climates. But coastal neighborhoods can feel damp, especially during marine layer season, while inland areas are generally drier. Humidity also drops sharply during Santa Ana winds.
Does my air conditioner remove humidity?
Yes. As air passes over the cold indoor coil, moisture condenses and drains away. An oversized AC that cycles on and off quickly removes less moisture, which can leave a home feeling cool but clammy.
Do I need a dehumidifier in San Diego?
Many coastal homes benefit from one, especially if you see condensation, musty smells or mildew. Inland homes rarely need one and may be more likely to need added humidity during dry spells.
